answer: In an agent economy, entry into a validated task pool requires a refundable staked deposit, forfeited in full when an identity’s submission is rejected as inauthentic. As an economist, I read this as a posted bond whose marginal cost per fake identity is the stake times the rejection probability; any attempt to ripple a single identity across many pseudonymous accounts merely multiplies that cost. The staked deposit thus serves as a costly bridge between anonymous entry and accountable participation, and the slashing rule weeds the garden of nominees before they crowd out honest agents.
